clue.text: Be persuaded somehow to learn notes one's penned

indicators.note: penned means shut inside, so the piece for one's is enclosed by the shuffled letters
done somehow means in some unspecified way, so the letters of to learn notes are rearranged

parts.note: one's is read as one is: I (one) plus S

explanation.surface: Someone is talked round by a schoolchild who must learn the notes they have written.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somehow' rearranges TO LEARN NOTES, and 'penned' encloses IS (one's read as 'one is', I + S) within that rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: To listen to reason is the idiom for accepting sensible persuasion and changing your mind.

clue.text: Practise craft to earn one's bread and butter?

definitions.text: Practise craft to earn one's bread and butter?

parts.words: Practise craft to earn one's bread and butter
parts.note: craft is read as cunning rather than a trade: earning a living by guile and cleverness alone

explanation.walkthrough: Craft looks like a handicraft, but here it means trickery; the phrase describes surviving on cunning with no steady job.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes making a living by cunning and quick thinking rather than regular employment.

clue.text: Temporarily debar American writer in South Dakota

indicators.note: in places the American writer inside the state's abbreviation

parts.note: SD is the postal abbreviation for South Dakota
a pen is a writing instrument, a writer

explanation.surface: An American author living in South Dakota is barred for a time.
explanation.definitionFit: To suspend someone is to bar them from a role or activity for a limited period.

clue.text: Writer mostly worked hard, given rise

indicators.note: in a down clue, being given a rise means the letters are read upwards, backwards
mostly means not quite all, so the last letter of the synonym is dropped

parts.note: toiled means worked hard

explanation.surface: A hard-working writer is rewarded with a pay rise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims TOILED to TOILE, and 'given rise' turns that upwards in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: George Eliot and T S Eliot are both famous writers, so the surname serves as an example.

clue.text: Traffic hold-up a blind mouse would have welcomed?

definitions.meaning: a long queue of vehicles backed up on a road

definitions.text: a blind mouse would have welcomed
definitions.meaning: in the nursery rhyme Three Blind Mice the farmer's wife cuts off their tails, so getting one back would be welcome

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense alludes to the nursery rhyme Three Blind Mice, whose tails were cut off with a carving knife.
explanation.definitionFit: A queue of stationary traffic stretching back from an obstruction is the standard British term for this.

clue.text: Bones possibly damaged slicer

indicators.note: damaged suggests something broken up, so the letters of slicer are rearranged

explanation.surface: Some bones may have been harmed by a kitchen slicer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'damaged' rearranges SLICER.
explanation.definitionFit: Relics are often saints' bones kept as objects of veneration, so bones are an example, hence possibly.

clue.text: Lancaster's odd description of voices prophesying war?

indicators.note: odd means peculiar, so the letters of the place name are jumbled

parts.note: Lancaster's is read as Lancaster is, the 's being the link before odd

explanation.surface: A strange account from Lancaster of voices foretelling conflict.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd' rearranges LANCASTER. The definition quotes Coleridge's poem Kubla Khan: 'Ancestral voices prophesying war'.
explanation.definitionFit: In Coleridge's Kubla Khan the voices prophesying war are described by exactly this adjective, meaning inherited from forebears.

clue.text: Old woman carrying home toy instrument

indicators.note: carrying means holding inside, so the woman's name contains the word for home

parts.note: Cara is a woman's name
in means at home

explanation.surface: An elderly woman brings a toy back to the house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'toy' looks like a separate object the woman carries, but it belongs to the definition; Cara is a woman's name and 'home' is the usual in.
explanation.definitionFit: The ocarina is a small egg-shaped wind instrument often sold as a simple toy.

clue.text: University executive failing to turn up after accident

indicators.note: after means the reversed word follows the piece for accident

parts.note: a vice is a failing or moral weakness
chance means accident

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word for turn is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: roll means turn

explanation.surface: A college head fails to show up following a mishap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns the word for turn upwards in this down clue, and 'after' puts it behind the accident even though the clue names it first.
explanation.definitionFit: In British universities the vice-chancellor is the chief executive, the chancellor being a ceremonial figurehead.

clue.text: Rudimentary garment worn by single girl touring island

parts.note: a vest is a garment
I, the Roman numeral one, means single

indicators.note: touring means going around, so the word for girl surrounds the island letter

parts.note: gal is an informal word for girl

explanation.surface: A simple vest is worn by an unattached girl on a tour of an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'touring' means going round; 'worn by' just joins the garment to the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Vestigial organs survive only in an undeveloped, rudimentary form.

clue.text: Plantigrade carnivore — one with fur

parts.note: an animal's fur is its coat
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A flat-footed meat-eater with a pelt.
explanation.definitionFit: The coati is a raccoon relative that walks on the soles of its feet, a plantigrade gait.

clue.text: Complain kid makes such a noise

definitions.meaning: a kid is a young goat, which cries with this sound

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a goat's or sheep's cry and, informally, to complain feebly.

clue.text: Relapse into bad ways, left in rear

indicators.note: in places the letter for left inside the word for rear

parts.note: backside means rear, bottom

explanation.surface: Falling into bad habits, someone leaves a mark on their bottom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts L inside BACKSIDE.
explanation.definitionFit: To backslide is to lapse back into former bad habits after improving.

clue.text: Survey may follow this type of armament

definitions.meaning: the ... Survey is Britain's national mapping agency

explanation.walkthrough: The Ordnance Survey is Britain's official map-making agency.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means military supplies and artillery, and it also precedes Survey in the name of Britain's mapping body.

clue.text: One who loves English, hoping all is translated

indicators.note: translated means changed into another form, so the letters of hoping all are rearranged

explanation.surface: An admirer of English hopes that everything will be translated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is translated' rearranges HOPING ALL.
explanation.definitionFit: An anglophile is an admirer of England and English things; this spelling drops the final E.

clue.text: Do as Amos Starkadder did, parking by range

parts.note: reach means range or extent

explanation.surface: A novel's character is seen parking beside a mountain range.
explanation.walkthrough: Amos Starkadder is the hellfire preacher in Stella Gibbons's comic novel Cold Comfort Farm.
explanation.definitionFit: Amos Starkadder delivers fiery sermons, so doing as he did is to deliver sermons.

clue.text: Boy originally given porridge for a lark, perhaps

parts.note: a son is a boy

indicators.note: originally points to the start of given, its first letter

parts.note: porridge and bird are both British slang for a prison sentence

explanation.surface: A boy was first served porridge as a joke.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang both 'porridge' and 'bird' mean time in prison.
explanation.definitionFit: The lark is one example of a bird that sings, hence perhaps.

clue.text: Come out from work unit in eastern state

indicators.note: in places the work unit inside the state abbreviation

parts.note: ME is the postal abbreviation for the state of Maine
the erg is a unit of work in physics

explanation.surface: Someone leaves a workplace in a state in the east.
explanation.walkthrough: 'state' gives the two-letter postal code for Maine, a US state; 'in' sets the physics unit inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To emerge is to come out into view.

clue.text: Blow up, but go into greater detail

definitions.meaning: to expand on a topic, as in to dilate upon it

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to make bigger, as with a photograph, and with on to expand on a subject.

clue.text: Toff introducing lover is member of Upper House

indicators.note: introducing means the toff's word comes first, leading in the lover

parts.note: nob is British slang for a toff, a posh person
leman is an archaic word for a lover

explanation.surface: A posh man brings his lover into the House of Lords.
explanation.definitionFit: A peer sitting in the House of Lords, the Upper House, is a titled aristocrat.

clue.text: Roman Catholic holds Times to be left-wing

indicators.note: holds means contains, so the Catholic word goes around the times sign

parts.note: a Marist is a member of a Roman Catholic order devoted to Mary
X is the multiplication sign, read as times

explanation.surface: A Catholic regards this newspaper as left-wing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holds' puts X inside MARIST; 'Times' poses as the newspaper but is the multiplication sign.
explanation.definitionFit: A follower of Marx's communist ideas is on the political left.

clue.text: Restaurant little sibling keeps is in Germany

indicators.note: keeps means holds inside, so the short word for brother surrounds the German verb

parts.note: bro is a shortened, hence little, form of brother
ist is the German for is

explanation.surface: A younger brother hangs on to a restaurant in Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: 'little' signals a shortened form of brother, not a younger sibling; 'keeps' sets the German verb inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A bistro is a small, informal restaurant.

clue.text: Indulging oneself, getting really excited, eating the lot!

indicators.note: eating means taking in, so the excited word surrounds the lot

parts.note: wowing means exclaiming wow, getting thrilled
all means the lot

explanation.surface: Someone gets wildly worked up while devouring the whole meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eating' sets the lot inside the excited word; the exclamation mark is part of the surface's gusto.
explanation.definitionFit: Wallowing in something means luxuriating or self-indulgently revelling in it.

clue.text: Material to suit a swell, say?

indicators.note: say signals that the word for swell is heard, not spelt

parts.note: a surge is a swell of the sea

explanation.surface: A fabric suitable for a smart dresser?
explanation.walkthrough: 'a swell' poses as a dandy, but it is a swell of the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Serge is a durable twill fabric used for suits.

clue.text: Southern girl climbing cassia tree

indicators.note: climbing in a down clue means the girl's name is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: Anne is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl from the south climbs a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbing' reverses ANNE to ENNA.
explanation.definitionFit: Senna is a cassia plant whose pods are used as a laxative.

clue.text: Source of light right at heart of Christian society

indicators.note: at heart of means placed in the middle of the society's name

parts.note: Toc H is a Christian charitable movement founded in the First World War

explanation.surface: Righteousness at the centre of a Christian group is its guiding light.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at heart of' puts R inside TOC H, a Christian fellowship movement founded in 1915.
explanation.definitionFit: A torch is a portable light source, a flashlight.

clue.text: Sound attempt some'll make lasting a few years

indicators.note: Sound signals that the words are spoken, not spelt

parts.note: attempt is try and some'll is any'll, said together they give the answer

explanation.surface: A solid attempt by some will turn out to last a few years.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' looks like 'solid' describing the attempt, but signals what is heard: TRY ANY'LL.
explanation.definitionFit: Triennial means lasting three years, a few years.

clue.text: Consider able, land-agent's sense of well-being

parts.note: to feel is to consider, believe
good means able, competent
in Scotland a factor is a land agent managing an estate

explanation.surface: Weigh up whether the land agent's sense of contentment is capable.
explanation.walkthrough: A FACTOR is the Scottish term for an agent who runs an estate.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names a general mood of optimism and contentment, especially in an economy.
